MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: The experience described in your resume will be evaluated and screened from the Office of Personnel Management's (OPMs) basic qualifications requirements. See: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/competency-based-policy/general-schedule/2200/2210-competency-based-policy/competency-based-qualification-standard/ for OPM qualification standards, competencies and specialized experience needed to perform the duties of the position as described in the MAJOR DUTIES and QUALIFICATIONS sections of this announcement by 10/29/2026 Applicant must have directly applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade (GG-13) in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: Supporting enterprise IT environment development and sustainment by applying knowledge of cloud and hosted applications; systems integration; application programming interfaces (APIs); identity, access, authentication, and authorization concepts; networking; cybersecurity principles; interoperability; data exchange; software deployment processes; or technical troubleshooting to translate customer needs into DCSA technical requirements and align stakeholders on technically supportable solutions. Assessing customer technical environments and requirements to identify technical constraints, dependencies, compatibility issues, or integration risks; clarify customer needs; and align those needs with technically supportable DCSA solutions and requirements. Conducting technical discovery; demonstrations; proof-of-concept and pilot activities; technical validation; deployment-readiness assessments; troubleshooting; or escalation support to facilitate shared understanding of technical requirements, solution capabilities, limitations, and implementation considerations. Translating customer technical needs into clear, actionable technical requirements for DCSA technical personnel, program stakeholders, or customer agencies to support effective coordination and mutual understanding. Explaining complex technical concepts, system capabilities, limitations, dependencies, or risks in plain language to customers and other non-technical audiences. Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies: Decision Making: Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Customer Service: Works with clients and customers to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Note: Clients and customers include any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government. Requirements Analysis: Knowledge of the principles and methods to identify, analyze, specify, design, and manage functional and infrastructure requirements; includes translating functional requirements into technical requirements used for logical design or presenting alternative technologies or approaches. Systems Integration: Knowledge of the principles, methods, and procedures for installing, integrating, and optimizing information systems components. Information Technology Test and Evaluation: Test, monitor and evaluate Information Technology technologies during design, development, procurement and/or implementation to ensure internal and external requirements are met. Leadership: Influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 2210, series as listed below: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations.

Details.JobSummary: DCSA's Office of Customer Success seeks a Success Engineer to serve as a technical advisor and strategic partner for high-visibility customer and mission-partner portfolios aligned to specific DCSA systems and services. You will lead technical engagement, solution adoption, and cross-functional integration; assess customer needs; identify implementation gaps and adoption barriers; and recommend actions to improve system use, service delivery, customer readiness, and mission outcomes.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission Through vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. The FY2026 - 2028 DCSA Strategic Execution Plan defines six strategic priorities for the agency: Deliver NBIS Deploy NI2 to Modernize Industrial Security Modernize and Sustain Trusted Workforce Determinations Rebuild the Workforce Compact Operate as a Customer-Centric Business Drive Audit-Ready Integration and Agency Efficiency with AI
MajorDuties: As a INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SPECIALIST (SUCCESS ENGINEER) you will be responsible for the following duties: - Serves as a senior technical advocate and technical translator within the Office of Customer Success (OCS), Enablement Division, bridging the gap between customer needs and DCSA technical capabilities for assigned enterprise portfolios, including NBIS, NI2, and other critical DCSA systems. - Supports Customer Executives, Account Managers, and customer-facing account teams by translating customer needs into detailed technical requirements and articulating those requirements to the appropriate DCSA technical and program stakeholders, identifying technical constraints and dependencies, and enabling more accurate alignment between customer expectations and DCSA technical solutions. - Leads proof-of-concept, pilot, and technical validation efforts across multiple stakeholders by assessing technical fit, configuring and validating use cases in test or demonstration environments, identifying integration and operational barriers, and helping ensure DCSA solutions are positioned to deploy correctly and demonstrate required value. - Explains system architectures, maps customer environments to DCSA solutions, reviews integration requirements, verifies application programming interface behavior, assesses configuration compatibility, evaluates interoperability considerations, tests technical workflows, and confirms deployment readiness criteria for assigned systems and portfolios. - Troubleshoots and helps resolve complex technical issues involving connectivity, configuration, APIs, identity and access dependencies, interoperability, and related operational factors affecting adoption, implementation, and customer success. - Coordinates with internal technical organizations, including system program offices, implementation teams, hosting and infrastructure teams, identity and access teams, help desk, operations and sustainment teams, and data and integration teams, to support technical planning, issue resolution, deployment readiness, and continuity of customer support. - Supports the full customer technical lifecycle, including pre-adoption technical enablement, onboarding and implementation activities during adoption, and post-deployment technical success and escalation management.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes for federal government positions need more detailed work descriptions and accomplishments than a typical private sector resume. Please be sure to clearly describe the full scope of your work experiences in your resume. Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail - experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service - experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication - briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving - identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions. In addition to the Basic Competency Requirements listed above: One year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade GS-11 in the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Specialized experience is defined as: Experience developing, implementing, coding, testing, operating, and modifying software and automated systems, and conducting systems requirement reviews; applying IT principles and practices in the software development process; experience using Common Business Oriented Language (COBOL) programming language to code and maintain software solutions. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You may qualify for consideration if meeting time-in grade, specialized experience, education requirement, 90 days after competitive appointment requirement, and all other qualification requirements within 30 calendar days after the closing date of the announcement, unless otherwise indicated on the announcement.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As the world's largest finance and accounting firm, the Defense Finance and Accounting Service (DFAS) pays all Department of Defense (DoD) military and civilian personnel, retirees and annuitants, and major DoD contractors and vendors. We take great pride in serving the men and women who serve America, and invite goal-oriented people like you to challenge yourself while providing a service to our nation. This position is being filled under the Direct Hire Authority for Certain Personnel of the Department of Defense via delegated authority by the Office of the Secretary of Defense. Positions may be filled as permanent or term with a full-time or part-time work schedule. Pay will vary by geographic location. We reserve the right to close this announcement early or to extend, as appropriate, based upon the needs of the Agency. Qualified application packages may be referred to management at various points in the selection process depending on the number and timing of applications received. Selections may be made at any point during the announcement open period. Veteran's Preference: Veteran's preference does not apply under this Direct Hire Authority (DHA).
MajorDuties: Provides development, implementation, operation, maintenance, and modification of major finance and/or accounting automation information systems to meet user needs and systems requirements.
Analyzes functional and technical requirements of IT systems to determine avenues of development or modification necessary to meet mission objectives.
Participates in systems requirement reviews and coordinates with customer to clarify requirements. Prepares system change/programming specifications, and specifies programming instructions.
Identifies alternative approaches to the design of current or proposed systems. Identifies how system modifications or new systems or subsystems affect current systems.

Prepares and executes tests for system or subsystem software validation. Reviews test results for effectiveness in meeting specifications and takes necessary corrective actions based on testing results.

Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Developing budget documentation and reports that comply with fiscal law and organizational financial management requirements; 2) Analyzing financial data to develop accurate forecasts, tracking obligations and expenditures; 3) Conducting regular reviews of IT portfolios to assess performance, value, and risks associated with IT investments; AND 4) Utilizing Information Technology Systems to route and track IT procurement requests. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-11). The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others; (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation; (3) Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. (4) Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. (5) Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. (6) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information; and (7) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate. (8) Teamwork - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. (9) Technical Competence - Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Develop, maintain, and update IT project plans, milestones, schedules, resource requirements, and risk-mitigation actions for assigned IT initiatives.
Coordinate IT project activities with stakeholders to achieve approved scope, schedule, cost, performance, and mission requirements.
Prepare project-status reports, decision papers, and briefings identifying project progress, resource requirements, issues, risks, and recommended courses of action for leadership.
Conduct regular reviews of the IT portfolio to assess the performance, value, costs, risks, and alignment of current and proposed IT investments with mission priorities.
Maintain complete and accurate IT portfolio documentation and project data in the approved portfolio-management system, including investment status, performance, cost, schedule, and risk information.
Analyze IT investment requirements and provide recommendations that align proposed solutions with organizational priorities, enterprise architecture, and applicable DoD requirements.
Develop IT acquisition-package documentation, including performance work statements, statements of requirements, independent Government cost estimates, and market-research documentation.
Prepare, route, track, and coordinate IT procurement requests through the approved IT acquisition process to obtain required technical, funding, and compliance approvals.
Coordinate with technical personnel, resource-management personnel, contracting officials, and other stakeholders to resolve IT acquisition issues and support timely procurement actions.
Monitor contractor performance and IT deliverables; identify deficiencies, coordinate corrective actions, and document results for technical and contracting stakeholders.
Prepare and coordinate IT purchase requests to help the organization obtain the right hardware, software, and services.
Evaluate vendor proposals and recommend IT products or services based on mission requirements, technical compatibility, cybersecurity considerations, performance standards, cost, and risk.

Attention to Detail- experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. In addition to the Basic Competency Requirements listed above, one year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade GS-11 in the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Specialized experience is defined as: Installing, configuring, testing and/or maintaining IT applications in accordance with customer needs and requirements; developing and analyzing product plans, release schedules, and product validity before release; and identifying, researching, and implementing emerging technology that enhances intranet and extranet capabilities. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. You may qualify for consideration if meeting time-in grade, specialized experience, education requirement, 90 days after competitive appointment requirement, and all other qualification requirements within 30 calendar days after the closing date of the announcement, unless otherwise indicated on the announcement.

Drug-Free Workplace Policy The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is committed to maintaining a safe, drug-free workplace. All DLA employees are required to refrain from illegal drug use on and off duty. DLA conducts pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and random drug testing. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. A negative drug test result must be received by HR within 30 calendar days after the EOD (i.e., start date). The selectee's inability successfully pass; or refusal to conduct the test may result in: 1) the tentative or FJO being withdrawn during the recruitment process; or 2) subsequently being removed from Federal service for failure to meet a condition of employment. You may be required to sign a "Drug Test Statement of Understanding" if you are selected for this position. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is illegal. MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: Supervisory Information Technology Specialist (Policy and Planning)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName: US Army Civilian Human Resources Agency
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current Civilian Employees of the Command Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Basic Requirement for Supervisory Information Technology Specialist (Policy and Planning) Specialized and Other Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes 1) Managing complex Information Technology (IT) projects, plans, and/or contracts; 2) Providing technical advice and guidance in various IT areas such as strategic planning, process improvements, and computer software/hardware design; 3) Coordinating with and providing status reports to senior leadership and stakeholders to ensure requirements are met; and/or 4) Developing new or modified IT system plans and policies to improve processes. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-13). The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: leading others by setting the standards for the quality of work, even in the most difficult and/or high pressure circumstances; reviewing and editing work completed by others to ensure that the quality of work meets acceptable work standards. (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: using expertise and experience to address complex problems, questions, or complaints; anticipating customer needs and modify the team's work activities, processes, and practices to meet these needs; collaborating across team and outside of own team to organize planning sessions that elicit ideas for improving customer service and support. (3) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: clearly explaining and defending complex ideas, appropriately adapting to each audience's level of knowledge; actively listening and clarifying points when presenting highly complex and controversial findings; using well-constructed, fact-based arguments to persuade stakeholders/officials to take action on suggestions for improvement. (4) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: providing precedent setting solutions to unique problems not previously encountered; helping team make decisions which are complicated by the number and nature of existing policy, guidelines, and organizational goals; identifying the root causes of problems; developing systemic solutions to address them and prevent them from reoccurring. Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-13).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position serves as a Supervisory Information Technology Specialist responsible for the management and operational control over critical Information Technology (IT) programs and projects. This announcement will be used to fill one position at various locations.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Provide expert technical and analytical advice in matters relating to information technology.
Design, schedule, and complete projects to meet user requirements utilizing structured design techniques.
Manage assigned information systems, networks, and facilities.
Analyze data on the information systems, identify causes of problems, and make recommendations for solutions.
Develop, assign, evaluate, and revise short and long-range objectives/goals for IT programs.

Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents), the responses you provide on the application questionnaire, and the result of the online assessments required for this position. You will be assessed on the following competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities, and other characteristics): Accountability Customer Service Decisiveness Flexibility Interpersonal Skills Problem Solving Resilience The USA Hire Assessments includes a cut score based on the minimum level of required proficiency in these critical general competencies. You must meet or exceed the cut score to be considered. You will not be considered for the position if you score below the cut score or fail to complete the assessment. Overstating your qualifications and/or experience in your application materials or application questionnaire may result in your removal from consideration. Cheating on the online assessment may also result in your removal from consideration. You may claim Military Spouse preference. You may claim Priority Placement Program (PPP) preference. Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP). If you are a Federal employee in the competitive service and your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority for this position. To receive selection priority, you must: (1) meet ICTAP eligibility criteria (2) be rated well-qualified for the position and; (3) submit the appropriate documentation to support your ICTAP eligibility. To be considered well-qualified and receive selection priority applicants must satisfy all qualification requirements for the position and receive a score of 90 or above. Additional information about the program is on OPM's Career Transition Resources website.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. Basic Requirements: Attention to Detail - experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been responsible for reviewing the work of others to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service - developing and maintaining relationships with customers, anticipating and assessing the current and future information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products or services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication - briefing senior-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of complex technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving - identifying alternatives to address unique, highly complex, or sensitive information technology-related issues. I have anticipated information technology-related problems and have identified and evaluated potential sources of information to generate alternative solutions. AND Qualifying Experience: To qualify at the GG-14, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service. For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: Supervising or leading employees responsible for delivering IT customer-support services, including planning work, establishing priorities, assigning workloads, providing technical guidance, and resolving operational issues; Managing IT customer-support operations involving troubleshooting, incident or service-request resolution, customer assistance, training, or service-delivery improvement; Managing IT projects or IT capability portfolios by coordinating customer requirements, technical teams, resources, schedules, risks, and delivery of IT services or products; and Developing, implementing, or interpreting IT customer-support policies, procedures, or service-delivery strategies to resolve complex IT problems and improve organizational performance Candidates must describe how they meet the qualifying experience and/or selective placement factor(s) within the body of their resume. All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: This position is being recruited under 10 USC 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It has been identified as a position necessary to carry out and support the mission of the US Cyber Command. It is in the Supervision/Management Work Category at the Senior Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure. It is located in the DISA - FE/Endpoint Svcs /Customer Spt Directorate.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: If you want to do interesting and challenging work and to make a contribution to national defense, DISA is a great place for you. DISA provides secure and reliable communications and computing support that enable the President and our military forces to communicate globally through voice, video, and data transmission. DISA is a leader within the Federal Government in implementing "people programs" and offers a broad range of quality-of-life and training programs. Go to www.disa.mil for more information. This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. Positions in the Cyber Excepted Service are positions necessary to carry out and support the mission of the United States Cyber Command.
MajorDuties: Directs and supervises customer-support personnel; plans work, assigns priorities, adjusts workloads, provides technical guidance, and resolves operational and personnel issues.
Manages planning and delivery of enterprise customer-support services, including troubleshooting, customer assistance, training, and resolution of complex IT service requirements.
Leads IT projects and portfolio activities; coordinates customer requirements, technical resources, schedules, risks, and service commitments to deliver mission capabilities.
Develops, interprets, and implements customer-support policies, procedures, and service-delivery strategies to improve performance and ensure consistent IT support.
Serves as a technical advisor on advanced IT customer-support issues; evaluates emerging technologies and resolves complex information-management and service-delivery problems.
Details.Education: There is no substitution of education for the qualifying experience at the GG-14 grade level.
Details.Evaluations: Once the application process is complete, a review of your resume and supporting documentation will be made and compared against your responses to the applicant questionnaire to determine if you are qualified for this job. Please follow all instructions carefully. Errors or omissions may affect your rating. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. For vacancies below the full-performance level of the position, the basic requirement will be evaluated on a developmental basis. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail - experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service - experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication - briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving - identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions. One year of specialized experience equivalent in level of difficulty and responsibility to that of the next lower grade (GS-11) within the federal service, which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Specialized Experience is defined as: Providing customer support and project reviews for information technology contingency planning initiatives; conducting technical Information Technology tasks and cybersecurity and technical assessments of planned and installed automated information systems. You may qualify for consideration if meeting specialized experience, education requirement, 90 days after competitive appointment requirement, and all other qualification requirements within 30 calendar days after the closing date of the announcement, unless otherwise indicated on the announcement. We may use this announcement to make a temporary promotion. For some positions, the temporary promotion may be made permanent without further competition. We may use this announcement to fill additional vacancies within 120 days of the closing date.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: All qualification and time-in-grade (if applicable) requirements must be met within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement. Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. For vacancies below the full-performance level of the position, the basic requirement will be evaluated on a developmental basis. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail- experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service- experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication- briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving- identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions. In addition to meeting the basic requirement, you must have one year specialized experience. NH-03: You must have one year of specialized experience at the next lover broadband NH-02, equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience must demonstrate support for RMF program support for information systems, including: Supporting RMF lifecycle activities, including categorization, control selection, control implementation, assessment preparation, authorization package development, and continuous monitoring. Familiarity with FedRAMP authorization, continuous monitoring, cloud security control implementation, shared responsibility models, and secure configuration practices for federal cloud environments. Preparing, reviewing, and maintaining RMF artifacts, including System Security Plans, control implementation statements, Security Assessment Reports, POA&Ms, risk acceptance documentation, assessment artifacts, and continuous monitoring records. Analyzing vulnerability scan results, configuration compliance data, audit findings, system changes, and assessment results to identify risk, support remediation, validate closure evidence, and document compensating controls. Practical understanding of Zero Trust architecture initiatives across ICAM, device compliance, network segmentation, application security, data, protection, telemetry, and automation pillars. NH-04: One year of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-03, equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience must demonstrate leadership or advisory responsibility for RMF program execution for complex, high-visibility, or enterprise information systems, including: Preparing, reviewing, and approving organizational cybersecurity and RMF policies, directives, procedures, and instructions to ensure alignment with federal, DoD, and organizational security requirements. Leading RMF planning, authorization readiness, control implementation reviews, assessment coordination, continuous monitoring, POA&M governance, risk acceptance analysis, and development of risk recommendations for leadership. Reviewing and validating authorization packages, security control evidence, vulnerability remediation strategies, cloud security responsibilities, system interconnections, software assurance results, and major system changes to determine cybersecurity risk and mission impact. Advising system owners, program managers, technical teams, assessors, contractors, and leadership on RMF execution, documentation quality, control implementation, audit readiness, vulnerability prioritization, Zero Trust alignment, and secure system lifecycle requirements. Leading cross-functional coordination across acquisition, engineering, operations, security, and executive stakeholders to resolve cybersecurity risks, support authorization decisions, maintain continuous monitoring visibility, and align RMF activities with mission priorities. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: NH03: This position serves as an Information System Security Officer (ISSO), supporting Risk Management Framework (RMF) execution for information systems through security control implementation and assessment, authorization package development, evidence collection, vulnerability tracking, Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) management, and continuous monitoring. Experienced in executing RMF activities for assigned information systems, applying cybersecurity principles, security controls, vulnerability management, continuous monitoring, and applicable federal, DoW, organizational, and Zero Trust requirements. Experienced in evaluating security control implementation and effectiveness; maintains authorization documentation; analyzes assessment evidence and findings; manages POA&Ms; and monitors security posture. Provides technical cybersecurity guidance and recommendations to system owners and stakeholders regarding security requirements, risks, controls, remediation, and authorization decisions. Experience in analyzing security documentation, vulnerability and configuration data, assessment findings, and system changes to identify security weaknesses, evaluate risk, and recommend remediation, mitigation, or compensation controls. Evaluates cybersecurity impacts of system changes and resolves or recommends solutions for complex issues involving vulnerabilities, control deficiencies, technical limitations, and competing mission and security requirements. Coordinates with technical stakeholders to validate remediation actions and security evidence and independently determines whether deficiencies have been adequately addressed. Evaluates cybersecurity practices and controls to identify gaps, risks, and improvement opportunities associated with Zero Trust, vulnerability management, continuous monitoring, and emerging cybersecurity requirements. Identifies recurring or systemic vulnerabilities and control weaknesses and recommends corrective actions or risk mitigation strategies. Develops technical analyses, risk assessments, metrics, reports, and briefings on system security posture, authorization status, vulnerabilities, remediation, and continuous monitoring results. NH04: This position serves as a senior ISSM and cybersecurity technical authority for a portfolio of complex, high-profile enterprise systems, programs, and modernization initiatives. Establishes technical priorities and governance for RMF execution, security controls, authorization readiness, continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, and POA&M oversight. Interprets and applies federal, DoW, organizational, and emerging cyber security requirements to resolve complex issues and ensure consistent risk management across the portfolio. Integrates cybers security risk information across systems and programs to identify significant or systemic weaknesses and mission impacts. Reviews and validates significant control deficiencies, remediation strategies, compensating controls, cloud security, system interconnections, software assurance, and major system changes. Develops risk-management strategies and recommendations for complex issues extending beyond the individual system level and advises leadership on authorization, operational, acquisition, and risk decisions. Advises senior leadership, system owners, program managers, and technical officials on cyber security risk, authorization readiness, vulnerability priorities, Zero Trust, cloud security, modernization, and emerging requirements. Leads integration of cyber security requirements and risk considerations across engineering, acquisition, operations, and program organizations to resolve significant cross-functional issues. Presents executive-level risk analyses, metrics, trends, and recommendations addressing portfolio security posture, systemic risks, and issues affecting mission execution. Certifications: Positions require a current cybersecurity certification appropriate to the role and grade level in alignment with DoD 8140 cyber workforce requirements, such as Security+, CySA+, CASP+, CISSP, CISM, or an equivalent ISSO/ISSM qualifying certification.

All experience areas shall additionally demonstrate each of the following competencies: 1) Attention to Detail, 2) Customer Service, 3) Oral Communication, and 4) Problem Solving.This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12). 1. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others. 2. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information. 4. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current USACE Employees with Competitive Status Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience GS-13: One year of specialized experience which includes:1) Serving as a subject matter expert on cyber security intelligence, performing activities to gather and preserve evidence on criminal or foreign intelligence entities to mitigate real-time threats and support the prosecution of computer crimes. 2) Analyzing computer-generated threats, log files, and collected evidence to identify network intruders, and fusing computer network attack analyses with criminal and counterintelligence investigations and operations. 3) Enhancing cyber security capabilities by evaluating security architectures, integrating security policy into IT systems, and managing the procurement and implementation of new security tools and systems in compliance with Department of Defense (DoD) and Army regulations. 4) Developing and presenting technical briefings, presentations, and reports on IT security status, weaknesses, and recommended courses of action to organizational leadership and external stakeholders. All experience areas shall additionally demonstrate each of the following competencies: 1) Attention to Detail, 2) Customer Service, 3) Oral Communication, and 4) Problem Solving. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12). The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others. (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation. (3) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information. (4) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate. Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-12).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position serves as an Information Technology Specialist (INFOSEC) for the US Army Corps of Engineers, acting as a subject matter expert on cyber security intelligence to enhance the organization's security posture. The role involves analyzing network threats, conducting counterintelligence and criminal investigations into computer intrusions, and implementing new security measures to protect IT systems.
Details.SubAgencyName: G-6 CYBER SECURITY DIRECTORATE CYBER NETWORK DEFENSE DIVISION
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Build Strong With Us at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), where engineering excellence meets public service. As the Nation's premier engineering, design, and construction management agency, we deliver innovative and efficient solutions that strengthen national security, support economic growth, and reduce disaster risks for communities across the country. At USACE, you will find meaningful work, collaborative teams, and opportunities to grow your career while making a lasting impact. We seek talented professionals with vision, creativity, leadership, and technical expertise to help solve some of the Nation's toughest engineering challenges. Build your purpose. Build your profession. Build your future. Discover why USACE is a great place to work and Build Strong With Us.
MajorDuties: Prepare and deliver technical presentations, engineering proposals, and after-action reports to inform leadership on the status of security projects.
Enhance cybersecurity capabilities by evaluating security architectures and managing the acquisition and implementation of new tools, systems, and software.
Fuse computer network attack analyses with criminal and counterintelligence investigations to support legal and operational actions.
Monitor external data sources to maintain an up-to-date understanding of cyber threat conditions and their potential impact on the enterprise.
Analyze computer-generated threats, log files, and collected evidence to identify the perpetrators of network intrusions.
Gather evidence on criminal or foreign intelligence entities to mitigate real-time threats and support the prosecution of computer crimes.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. In addition to meeting the basic requirement, applicants must possess qualifying experience. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service. Basic Requirements: Attention to Detail - experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been responsible for reviewing the work of others to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service - developing and maintaining relationships with customers, anticipating and assessing the current and future information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products or services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication - briefing senior-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of complex technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving - identifying alternatives to address unique, highly complex, or sensitive information technology-related issues. I have anticipated information technology-related problems and have identified and evaluated potential sources of information to generate alternative solutions. Qualifying Experience: To qualify at the GG-15 grade level, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service. For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: Experience managing mission partner outreach and relationships; OR managing enterprise-wide governance; OR synchronizing mission partner efforts to increase operational effectiveness. Candidates must describe how they meet the qualifying experience and/or selective placement factor(s) within the body of their resume. All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: This position is being recruited under 10 USC 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It has been identified as a position necessary to carry out and support the mission of the US Cyber Command. It is in the Supervision/Management Work Category at the Expert Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure. It is located in the DISA ACQ/PAE MISSION PARTNER ENV (ME931).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: If you want to do interesting and challenging work and to make a contribution to national defense, DISA is a great place for you. DISA provides secure and reliable communications and computing support that enable the President and our military forces to communicate globally through voice, video, and data transmission. DISA is a leader within the Federal Government in implementing "people programs" and offers a broad range of quality-of-life and training programs. Go to www.disa.mil for more information. This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. Positions in the Cyber Excepted Service are positions necessary to carry out and support the mission of the United States Cyber Command.
MajorDuties: Exercises responsibility for the overall management of functions and staff required to support the mission partner outreach, initial requirements definition/analysis, and customer relationship management for assigned Mission Partners.

Performs information technology (IT) project business management duties; focusing and synchronizing DISA and customer efforts to achieve goals and increase operational effectiveness through a unified enterprise-wide project management approach.
Meets with key customer and coordinating officials to assess customer satisfaction, explains organization policies and procedures, and resolves problems that arise.
Participates in special projects and initiatives and performs special assignments.

Develops Mission Partner portfolios and strategic plans to assist the mission partner in the oversight and financial management of existing capabilities, as well as the planning and delivery of future requirements.
Details.Education: There is no substitution of education for the qualifying experience at the GG-15 grade level. Please Note: This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. If you are a current Federal Career/Career-Conditional employee, you will be placed on an Excepted appointment. This appointment does not confer eligibility to be non-competitively converted to an appointment in the competitive service.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/competency-based-policy/general-schedule/2200/2210-competency-based-policy/competency-based-qualification-standard/ BASIC REQUIREMENT OR INDIVIDUAL OCCUPATIONAL REQUIREMENT: OPM: General Schedule Qualification Standard for Information Technology (IT) Management Series, 2210 (Alternative A)Experience must be IT related; the experience may be demonstrated by paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training (for example, IT certification), as appropriate GS-5 through GS-15 (or equivalent): For all positions individuals must have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the four competencies listed below. The employing agency is responsible for identifying the specific level of proficiency required for each competency at each grade level based on the requirements of the position being filled. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately . Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: AND SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02 or equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 in the Federal Service. Specialized experiences includes: Planning, coordinating, and installing applications software and hardware operation systems. Administering and maintaining assigned systems. Providing technical guidance and instructions to users and other IT specialists. Troubleshooting complex problems and providing support in a manner that minimizes interruptions in customer's work process. Maintaining liaison with manufacturers, professional organizations, and counterparts at other installations and services regarding technologies and advancements, and participating as a key senior member and advisor on special committees and special projects designed to study methods to enhance the use of information technology throughout installations. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of the principles, methods, and practices for integrating information system components sufficient to plan, coordinate, and administer computer systems, and optimize system performance. Knowledge of the latest advancements in technology to initiate corrective or preventative action to ensure optimum performance of the system. Knowledge of performance tuning tools, database management, and project management methods sufficient to optimize systems performance, troubleshoot database performance problems, and perform a wide range of systems administration functions. Knowledge of operating systems, associated devices, and the interoperability of systems sufficient to install, upgrade, troubleshoot, test, and maintain those systems; to optimize the functionality and performance of systems; and to ensure the availability, integrity, efficiency, and reliability of servers. Ability to apply methods and practices for troubleshooting, recovering, adjusting, modifying, and improving systems to solve complex problems, provide support that minimizes interruptions in service to customers, and maintain liaison with industry and other activities to provide awareness of state-of-the-art technology. Ability to communicate orally and in writing. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.
